b: Recently I heard an advisor tout the benefits of "direct indexing". This concept is for index fund investors who want to be able to time and take tax losses from sales of individual stock. You basically replicate an index by owning say, shares in 500 companies instead of an S&P 500 index fund.
Does this make sense? Couldn't you still own the index fund and own shares in just a few companies to occasionally take tax losses, assuming it was worth it for such losses.
Owning shares in 500 companies seems a preposterous way to get the benefits of indexing. What say you?
